newsitem.title: CROATIA: Yugoslavia hands over files on missing.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia hands over files on missing.

text.p: Yugoslavia has handed over to Croatia some 500 files on missing persons in what appears to be a warming up in relations between the two countries, international human rights officials said on Friday.

Mark Steinberg of International Commission for Missing Persons (ICMP) told Croatian television Yugoslavia had handed over dossiers on the people whose remains were found in the town of Vukovar in 1991 upon its fall to beseiging Serb forces.
"Representatives of Croatia and Yugoslavia reported what they characterised as good progress in their relationship," Steinberg said.
He also said Yugoslavia promised to deliver hundreds of the files on the missing people still sought by Croatia.
ICMP, headed by former U.S. Secretary of State Cyrus Vance, has been set up to aid search of people who went missing during the 1991-95 war that followed the breakup of former Yugoslavia.
It met with government representatives of Croatia, Yugoslavia and Bosnia's Moslem and in Zagreb on Friday.
Croatia has often accused Yugoslavia of witholding the information on the missing and delaying the handover of the documentation.
Croatian radio said Bosnia filed 18,985 missing persons requests but ICMP was able to solve only 1,085 of such cases.
It also solved approximately half of the 3,458 requests filed by Croatia.
